lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The EXPERIENCE entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: The 2025 Lumen Travel role appears after a role that ended in 2024, so a reader may miss the more recent position.

items.says: EDUCATION appears before EXPERIENCE instead of leading with relevant web-development work.
items.because: A reader has to pass the education section before reaching the strongest evidence of professional work.

items.says: The line names ownership but not a concrete contribution to the websites or component library.
items.because: The web-development work behind the responsibility is unclear.

items.says: The line does not say what value the websites or component library delivered.
items.because: Without an outcome, the importance of the work is hard to assess.

items.says: The interview-and-preview result should appear before the other bullets in this entry.
items.because: Its concrete reduction in broken pages is less likely to be noticed later in the entry.

items.says: “Reported by students” adds detail after the key reduction without clarifying the result.
The search-time figures do not identify what was timed.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what task or measure improved.

items.says: The 35% performance improvement does not identify its metric or comparison point.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what improved or assess the result without a baseline.

items.says: The LCP reduction is incorrectly attributed to lazy-loading the hero image.
items.because: Delaying the fetch of the LCP image does not explain an improvement in LCP.

items.says: Storing input in React state and rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML does not prevent cross-site scripting.
items.because: React state does not sanitize input, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses normal escaping.

items.says: The XSS-prevention claim gives no check or evidence that prevention was established.
items.because: The implementation description alone does not show that the security outcome was tested or verified.

items.says: The hotel-search result should appear before the other bullets in this entry.
items.because: Its technical rebuild and outcomes would be easier to notice first.

items.says: The line does not explain how the app gets or updates live arrival data.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what integration or implementation made the central feature possible.

items.says: “Against 2.9s before” presents the earlier load time awkwardly.
The open-source release and agency link do not show your technical contribution to the app.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what you built or how you contributed technically.

items.says: The bullet’s React claim conflicts with the project heading’s Vue label.
items.because: The reader cannot tell which framework the project used.

items.says: The booking-flow bullet gives no outcome for the work.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what the frontend contribution enabled or improved.

items.says: “Worked on the frontend” does not name a specific action.
The calendar bullet should appear before the other bullets in this entry.
items.because: Its specific component and difficult cases would be easier to notice first.

items.says: The calendar component and tests have no stated outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what the component enabled or what the tests helped prevent.

items.says: The booking increase does not identify the booking measure or period compared.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what “about a tenth” measures or evaluate the comparison.

items.says: The load-time and booking outcomes appear after the implementation detail instead of leading the bullet.
items.because: Leading with the outcomes would make the impact easier to scan.

items.says: The travel-search bullet does not belong under Library Room Booking and appears to duplicate the Lumen Travel achievement.
items.because: The library project contains a travel-search result, making the achievement look misattributed or repeated.

items.says: “Storybok” is a misspelling of “Storybook.”
items.because: It can distract a reader and make the tool harder to recognize.

items.says: Angular is listed without support elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: No experience or project shows Angular in use, so a reader may question the hands-on experience behind the skill.
